4.column:
Devin takes Week 4 at 12–4 on the tiebreaker. He and Nate V both rode the Falcons, Atlanta hung 45 on the Saints, and the 69 total made Devin's 47 a lot less wrong than Nate's 38. Nate goes home 12–4 with nothing but the receipt. Dan, Peggy and Thom finished a game back at 11–5. The collapse belongs to Mike Sombloski, tied for the lead at 9–2 Sunday evening and 1–4 from there to finish 10–6. The dumbest pick goes to Jeff G, the only soul on the Dolphins, who scored ten. Twenty-two of you took the Bills against New England; Andy R took the Patriots alone and is insufferable today, deservedly.

Mrs. Sombloski wrote down 67 for the tiebreaker. Six seven. The game landed on 69, two off, the closest guess in the room, attached to a sheet with six picks on it. Respect the bit.

5.column:
Ryan Holovics wins Week 5 at 12–2 and takes the $95 pot. He clinched it Sunday, then celebrated by taking the Rams on Monday; Buffalo won 37–34 in overtime, so even the champ leaves with a fresh bruise. Tom finishes alone in second at 11–3, close enough to smell the money, far enough to get none of it. The commissioner sits in a nine-way pileup at 10–4, bonnet still on.

The collapse belongs to Walczyk: 4–10, tied for dead last with the house, and the house was picking with a coin. Dumbest pick goes to Leah and Mrs. Sombloski, the only two on the Titans, who scored three points. Mike Sombloski went 10–4; Mrs. Sombloski went 6–8 and lost the feud by four. Derek asked everyone to root for Ariel not to finish last. She went 8–6, nowhere near it. The Monday total landed on 71, and Nate V's 69 was closest in the room, which bought him exactly nothing.

6.column:
Ryan Holovics goes back-to-back: 10–4, $95, on the tiebreaker. His 52 missed Monday's 40 by twelve; B-rad's 54 missed by fourteen. Mrs. Sombloski also went 10–4, then guessed 67 like she was betting on a basketball game. He asked if we'd let him play again after last week's beating. We did. He did it again.

Best story of the night: Ariel called the total dead on, 40 exactly, and went 6–8 doing it. Perfect tiebreaker, no record to hang it on. Dumbest pick goes to Thom, the only sheet on the Raiders; Buffalo still won, barely. Derek announced "This is my week" and went 7–7, same as the commissioner, Walczyk and half the room. The Sombloski feud flips: Mrs. 10–4, Mike 7–7, still on the floor. Claude finished 8–6 and its Lock, the Rams, lost to Arizona. Five of you beat the bot. The rest of you lost to a spreadsheet.

7.columnHead: Ryan again. Seven-way tie, one tiebreaker, same guy.
7.column:
Seven sheets finished 9–5 — Ryan, Josh, Devin, Derek, Andy R, Arod and the house — and the Cowboys settled it 38–21, 59 points that blew past every guess in the room. Ryan's 52 was closest by four, so the man who asked how long you'd keep letting him take his money is back-to-back champ. Andy R called the league rigged and then guessed 37. The commissioner says it isn't rigged; the commissioner also went 7–7.

Dumbest pick goes to the house, which made the Texans, 10.5-point favorites, its Lock of the Week and watched the Giants walk out 27–21. Thom, Nate V and Mrs. Sombloski saw it coming; nobody else did. Mike Sombloski, whose exit polls had him up, went 4–10 and owns the cellar outright. Josh's Bertburgers stay in the freezer. Got a question for the commissioner? Ask it on the pick sheet.

8.columnHead: Commissioner files, begs the room to beat Ryan
8.column:
Three sheets in, and the theme is unanimous: Ryan. Kaylani & Luka opened with "Ryan is going down," and the commissioner followed with "Someone please beat Ryan," which is less a threat than a man filing a missing-persons report for his own pool. Mrs. Sombloski filed without a word, which still beats anything Mike has said since his 4–10.

Ryan, the back-to-back champ, hasn't filed, so the whole room is yelling at an empty chair. Mike hasn't either; the cellar keeps the lights on. Andy R still hangs on the mugshot for calling the league rigged, courtesy of Ryan. Thursday in Green Bay locks the first game. Got a question for the commissioner? Ask it on the pick sheet.
